intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush jungle and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group classes here, blending breathwork and asana with Bali's natural beauty. A deeply restorative and affordable experience.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-friendly surf lesson on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful stretches of coastline. After your lesson, relax and watch the legendary Bali sunset with a fresh coconut in hand. Instructors are widely available directly on the beach.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Bali's world-famous wellness culture at The Yoga Barn in Ubud. Drop into daily classes covering Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, and meditation. The lush jungle setting and community atmosphere make this a highlight for any yoga-focused traveler. Drop-in classes are affordable and schedules are flexible.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Crystal-Clear Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at Nusa Dua's pristine white-sand beaches, known for calm turquoise waters perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Rent a sun lounger, explore the coral reefs just offshore, and enjoy fresh grilled seafood from beachside warungs. A quintessential Bali beach escape.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Ubud Market Tour
experiences.description: Start your morning at the vibrant Ubud Traditional Market to source fresh local ingredients, then head to a family-run cooking school to prepare authentic Balinese dishes like satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding. A perfect blend of culture, food, and hands-on experience that deepens your connection to the island.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort (Beachfront, Bali). Freshen up, unpack, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Indian Ocean and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach in front of the resort. Explore the nearest beach strip for local warungs (small eateries) and night stalls.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport or on the plane before landing
meals.lunch: Quick and affordable nasi goreng or mie goreng at a local warung near the resort (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.dinner: Beachside warung dinner — try grilled fish with steamed rice and sambal (~IDR 50,000–70,000)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some currency at the airport for better rates. Avoid taxis from the airport without negotiating a fixed price or use a ride-hailing app like Grab or Gojek to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a free or donation-based sunrise yoga session on the beach (many resorts and local instructors offer early morning sessions). Enjoy the warm 25°C morning air and gentle sea breeze.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local beach — rent a surfboard or bodyboard for a couple of hours (~IDR 50,000–80,000/hour). Alternatively, simply swim and relax on the sand. Visit a nearby surf school for a beginner group lesson (~IDR 150,000–200,000).
day_by_day.evening: Wander to a nearby night market or local street food area. Try various Indonesian snacks like satay, pisang goreng (fried banana), and fresh coconut water.

meals.breakfast: Warung breakfast of bubur ayam (chicken porridge) or nasi kuning with tea (~IDR 20,000–35,000)
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit bowl or gado-gado from a beach warung (~IDR 30,000–45,000)
meals.dinner: Night market street food spread — mix of satay, tempeh, and rice (~IDR 40,000–60,000)

day_by_day.notes: Apply sunscreen generously — the Bali sun is strong even at 25°C. Bring a reusable water bottle to stay hydrated and reduce plastic waste.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga class at a budget-friendly local studio near the resort (~IDR 80,000–120,000 per drop-in class). Many studios offer multi-class passes for better value. Hatha or Vinyasa flow classes are widely available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Hindu temple (such as a local sea temple or pura) — most are free or ask for a small donation. Rent a sarong at the entrance (~IDR 10,000–20,000) if you don't have one. Explore the temple grounds and learn about Balinese Hindu culture.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Balinese massage at a budget spa near the resort (~IDR 80,000–120,000 for a 60-minute session). This is a wonderful way to recover after a day of activity.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or toast with local jam at a budget café (~IDR 35,000–55,000)
meals.lunch: Nasi campur (mixed rice with various sides) at a local warung (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.dinner: Grilled corn, satay lilit (Balinese minced fish satay), and rice at a local restaurant (~IDR 50,000–75,000)

day_by_day.notes: When visiting temples, dress modestly — cover shoulders and knees. A sarong and sash are usually provided or available to rent at the entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach walk along the shoreline to collect shells and enjoy the calm ocean. Practice some self-guided meditation or stretching on the sand. The warm summer weather makes early mornings especially pleasant.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a Grab/Gojek ride to a popular nearby beach known for snorkeling. Rent snorkeling gear (~IDR 50,000–75,000) and explore the colorful coral reefs and marine life. Many beaches have budget rental shops along the shore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Attend a free or low-cost Kecak fire dance performance if available nearby (~IDR 100,000–150,000 for ticketed shows at cultural venues).

meals.breakfast: Banana pancakes — a Bali backpacker classic — at a local café (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or quick warung meal near the snorkeling beach (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Local Balinese restaurant — try babi guling (suckling pig) if budget allows, or opt for ayam betutu (slow-cooked spiced chicken) (~IDR 60,000–90,000)

day_by_day.notes: Snorkeling is best in the morning when the water is calm and visibility is highest. Bring an underwater phone case or waterproof bag for your valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Join a group yoga class focusing on breathwork and pranayama at a local studio (~IDR 80,000–100,000). This is a great mid-trip reset. Many Bali studios offer classes in open-air bamboo pavilions for an immersive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local art market or crafts village nearby. Browse handmade batik clothing, silver jewelry, wood carvings, and paintings. Practice your bargaining skills — prices are often negotiable. Budget for small souvenirs (~IDR 50,000–200,000 depending on items).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails (or fresh juice for budget-conscious travelers) at a beachfront café. Watch the sky turn orange and pink over the ocean — one of Bali's most iconic experiences.

meals.breakfast: Jajan pasar (traditional Balinese rice cakes and sweets) from a local market stall (~IDR 15,000–25,000)
meals.lunch: Warung lunch — lawar (Balinese mixed vegetable and meat salad) with rice (~IDR 30,000–45,000)
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood BBQ on the beach — choose your fish, prawn, or squid by weight and have it grilled (~IDR 70,000–120,000)

day_by_day.notes: At art markets, always smile and be friendly when bargaining — it's part of the culture. Aim to pay about 50–60% of the initial asking price as a starting point.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or scooter (~IDR 50,000–80,000/day for bicycle; ~IDR 70,000–100,000/day for scooter) and explore the surrounding countryside or coastal roads. Visit nearby rice paddies or local villages for authentic Balinese scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a quiet beach cove or hidden beach accessible by scooter. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and reading. With 30mm rain expected this month, afternoons may occasionally have brief showers — bring a light rain jacket.
day_by_day.evening: Cook your own meal or join a budget cooking class (~IDR 150,000–250,000) to learn how to make traditional Balinese dishes like sate, lawar, and jaje (desserts).

meals.breakfast: Nasi goreng with a fried egg and krupuk (crackers) at the resort or nearby warung (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.lunch: Roadside warung discovery — stop wherever looks busy with locals for the freshest, cheapest food (~IDR 20,000–35,000)
meals.dinner: Home-cooked Balinese meal from your cooking class, or a simple warung dinner (~IDR 40,000–60,000)

day_by_day.notes: If renting a scooter, ensure you have an international driving permit and always wear a helmet. Bali traffic can be chaotic — drive cautiously, especially on narrow roads.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint rest and wellness day. Start with a 90-minute yin yoga or restorative yoga session at a nearby studio (~IDR 100,000–130,000). Focus on stretching and relaxation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local waterfall or natural pool if accessible from your area (many are within 30–60 minutes by scooter). Entry fees are typically ~IDR 10,000–20,000. Take a refreshing dip in the natural pool.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a full-body Balinese traditional massage and flower bath at a mid-range spa (~IDR 150,000–200,000 for a package). A well-deserved halfway-through-the-trip reward.

meals.breakfast: Açaí bowl or yogurt with granola and tropical fruit at a health café (~IDR 45,000–65,000)
meals.lunch: Tempeh and tofu stir-fry with steamed rice at a vegetarian-friendly warung (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.dinner: Romantic budget dinner at a candlelit beachfront warung — grilled fish, vegetables, and rice (~IDR 60,000–80,000)

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to do laundry at a local laundry service (~IDR 10,000–15,000 per kg) and restock any essentials like sunscreen, insect repellent, or snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach yoga — either self-practice or join a free community yoga session on the beach if available. The warm 25°C mornings are perfect for outdoor practice with ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local fishing village nearby. Watch traditional Jukung (outrigger fishing boats) come in with the morning catch. Chat with locals and learn about their way of life. This is a free and authentic cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local night market (pasar malam) for dinner and entertainment. Try as many street foods as possible — this is the most budget-friendly and delicious way to eat in Bali.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit platter (papaya, mango, pineapple, dragon fruit) from a market stall (~IDR 15,000–25,000)
meals.lunch: Babi guling (suckling pig) or nasi campur at a popular local spot (~IDR 40,000–60,000)
meals.dinner: Night market feast — sample 4–5 different dishes for a total of ~IDR 50,000–80,000

day_by_day.notes: Bring small denomination bills (IDR 5,000–20,000 notes) to the night market for easy transactions. Most stalls don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip by shared minivan or Grab to a famous nearby beach or surf spot (e.g., a neighboring bay or surf break). Enjoy a morning surf session or simply watch the surfers from the shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore clifftop viewpoints near the beach area for dramatic ocean views and photo opportunities. Many are free to access. Walk along coastal paths and enjoy the warm summer breeze.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Attend a free Balinese ceremony or temple festival if one is happening nearby — ask your hotel staff about local events. These are deeply spiritual and culturally rich experiences.

meals.breakfast: Quick warung breakfast before departure — fried rice or noodles with tea (~IDR 20,000–35,000)
meals.lunch: Beach warung at the day trip destination — fresh coconut and grilled corn (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner back near the resort — try a new warung you haven't visited yet (~IDR 50,000–70,000)

day_by_day.notes: Shared transport (bemo or tourist shuttle buses) is much cheaper than private taxis for day trips. Book through your hotel or a local travel agent for the best rates.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated yoga and meditation morning — find a 2-hour workshop or masterclass at a local yoga shala (~IDR 120,000–180,000). Focus on deepening your practice with an experienced Balinese or international instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or permaculture garden if available in the area. Many offer free or low-cost tours and sell fresh produce. Pick up healthy snacks for the rest of the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Beach bonfire (if permitted) or gather with fellow travelers at a budget beachside bar. Enjoy Bintang beer (~IDR 35,000–50,000) or fresh lime juice (~IDR 15,000–25,000) while watching the stars.

meals.breakfast: Healthy smoothie and avocado toast at a budget health café (~IDR 40,000–60,000)
meals.lunch: Farm-fresh salad and organic rice bowl at the farm visit or a nearby café (~IDR 45,000–65,000)
meals.dinner: Beachside BBQ — choose from a selection of meats, fish, and vegetables grilled to order (~IDR 60,000–90,000)

day_by_day.notes: Bali has a thriving yoga community with workshops happening almost daily. Check local notice boards at cafés and studios for upcoming events, many of which are donation-based.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling or freediving trip arranged through a local dive shop (~IDR 150,000–250,000 for a guided snorkel trip including gear). Explore vibrant coral gardens and spot tropical fish, sea turtles, and rays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxing afternoon by the pool or on the beach. Read, journal, or simply rest. With warm 25°C weather, this is the perfect lazy afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local area on foot for last-minute souvenir shopping. Look for handmade goods directly from artisans for better prices and a more meaningful purchase.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the water activity — banana and granola bar (~IDR 10,000–20,000)
meals.lunch: Post-snorkeling warung meal — nasi goreng or mie goreng with fresh juice (~IDR 30,000–45,000)
meals.dinner: Special budget splurge dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant — try a Balinese rijsttafel (rice table) set menu (~IDR 100,000–150,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book snorkeling trips in advance or the evening before to secure a spot. Morning trips offer the best visibility and calmest water conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga session on the beach — a peaceful and reflective practice to appreciate your last full day in Bali. Set intentions for carrying your wellness practices home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a final leisurely afternoon at your favorite beach spot discovered during the trip. Swim, sunbathe, and take photos. Visit any places you may have missed or want to revisit.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best local warung you discovered during your trip. Treat yourself to your favorite Balinese dishes one last time. Share stories with fellow travelers if you've made friends along the way.

meals.breakfast: Special breakfast treat — full Indonesian breakfast spread at a local café (~IDR 45,000–65,000)
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — fresh coconut, fruit, and a sandwich or wrap (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Farewell Balinese feast — your personal favorites from the trip (~IDR 70,000–100,000)

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight and set aside any items you want to donate (clothes, books, etc.) to local charities or leave for the hotel staff. Keep departure essentials easily accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali — wake up early for one last beach walk and sunrise. Take in the sights, sounds, and smells of the island one final time. Do a short 20-minute meditation or stretching session on the sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort. Depending on your departure flight time, explore any last-minute sights near the hotel or head to the airport. Use Grab or Gojek for affordable airport transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, yoga, culture, and delicious food. Carry the Balinese spirit of 'Tri Hita Karana' (harmony with God, people, and nature) home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final nasi goreng or banana pancakes at a beloved warung (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.lunch: Airport meal or last warung stop before heading to the airport (~IDR 40,000–70,000)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2–3 hours before international flights. Declare any food items or wooden goods at customs. Keep some IDR for airport snacks or last-minute purchases — unused IDR can be exchanged back at the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali (flight lands at 13:00) — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Ngurah Rai International Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort (~45 min). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room. Take a leisurely first stroll along the beach in front of the resort to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the resort beach or nearby beachfront promenade. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's beachside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport — try a local warung (food stall) for nasi goreng or mie goreng (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Resort beachside restaurant — grilled seafood platter and fresh coconut water (~IDR 150,000–250,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Hydrate well and avoid overplanning. Exchange some currency at the airport for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Bali mornings right with a sunrise beach yoga session on the resort beach or at a nearby beachfront yoga studio. Many studios in Bali offer drop-in classes (~IDR 100,000–150,000). Breathe in the warm sea air and ease into your trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach area — rent a sun lounger, swim in the warm Indian Ocean, and snorkel along the reef if accessible near the resort. Alternatively, rent a bicycle and explore the coastal village nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a popular nearby beach bar or warung for a casual sunset drinks session. Explore the night market if one is nearby for local street food.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a local café — fresh tropical fruit, eggs, and Balinese black rice pudding (~IDR 50,000–80,000)
meals.lunch: Beachside warung — grilled fish with steamed rice and sambal, fresh young coconut (~IDR 60,000–100,000)
meals.dinner: Local night market or beachside restaurant — satay skewers, gado-gado, and fresh fruit juice (~IDR 80,000–150,000)

day_by_day.notes: Apply sunscreen generously — the Bali sun is strong even in warm summer weather. Bring a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga class at a well-regarded local studio (look for Vinyasa or Hatha flow sessions). Afterward, visit a nearby temple such as Tanah Lot or a local sea temple for a cultural morning — dress respectfully with a sarong (often provided at temple entrances).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a guided snorkeling or stand-up paddleboard (SUP) lesson at the beach (~IDR 200,000–350,000 for lessons or rentals). The calm afternoon waters are ideal for beginners and intermediates.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional Balinese massage at a local spa (~IDR 120,000–200,000 for 60 min). Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the resort area.

meals.breakfast: Local café — avocado toast or acai bowl with Balinese coffee (~IDR 70,000–120,000)
meals.lunch: Beachside café — chicken or tofu wrap, fresh juice (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant — Balinese babi guling (suckling pig) or vegetarian rendang with steamed rice (~IDR 150,000–250,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book yoga classes and spa treatments in advance during peak season. Carry a sarong for temple visits.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud — hire a private driver (~IDR 400,000–600,000 for the day, highly recommended). Start with the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in Ubud. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's vibrant art market for handmade crafts, textiles, and souvenirs. Visit the Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) and stroll the main street. Stop at a traditional Balinese cooking class if available (~IDR 350,000–500,000).
day_by_day.evening: Watch a traditional Kecak fire dance performance at Uluwatu Temple or in Ubud (~IDR 100,000–150,000 per person) — a truly unforgettable Balinese cultural experience. Return to the resort by private driver.

meals.breakfast: Resort or hotel café before departure
meals.lunch: Ubud warung — nasi campur (mixed rice plate) with local vegetable dishes (~IDR 50,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Ubud restaurant before heading back — duck confit Balinese style (bebek betutu) or vegan bowl (~IDR 150,000–220,000)

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is about 1–1.5 hours from most coastal areas. Start early to maximize time. Bring cash as not all Ubud vendors accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise yoga or meditation session on the beach. Afterward, take a long peaceful walk along the coastline, exploring rock formations, hidden coves, or tide pools depending on your resort's location.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby surf school for a beginner or intermediate surf lesson (~IDR 250,000–400,000 including board rental and instructor). Bali's waves are ideal for learning in July.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort pool or beach. Enjoy a quiet dinner at a beachfront restaurant with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Healthy smoothie bowl or eggs Benedict at a local café (~IDR 70,000–120,000)
meals.lunch: Post-surf warung — nasi goreng with fried egg, iced tea (~IDR 50,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant — grilled barramundi with lemongrass and coconut rice (~IDR 180,000–280,000)

day_by_day.notes: Check surf conditions with your instructor. Even beginners can enjoy gentle waves in Bali. Wear reef shoes if the beach has coral.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the stunning Tegallalang Rice Terraces (if accessible as a day trip) — a UNESCO-listed landscape. Walk the trails through the lush green terraces in the cool morning air. Arrive before 9am to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a local coffee plantation en route back — try the famous Kopi Luwak (civet coffee) and sample various Balinese teas and coffees. Browse the plantation's gift shop for quality local coffee to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Treat yourself to a couples or solo spa package — traditional Balinese boreh body scrub and floral bath (~IDR 300,000–450,000). Light dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — grab a local bakery pastry and Balinese coffee to go (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.lunch: Warung near the rice terraces — mixed satay plate with peanut sauce and rice (~IDR 70,000–100,000)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — light pasta or salad with fresh tropical fruit dessert (~IDR 130,000–200,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Tegallalang terraces can be busy by mid-morning. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a hat. Some areas charge a small entrance fee (~IDR 20,000–50,000).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day — sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and practice self-guided morning yoga or stretching on your private balcony or the resort beach. Read a book, journal, or simply enjoy the sound of the waves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby beach that's different from your resort beach — rent a scooter or hire a driver for a short trip. Consider visiting a quieter, less-touristy stretch of coastline for swimming and relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Join a group sunset yoga class on the beach (~IDR 100,000–150,000) followed by a social dinner at a popular local restaurant. Great opportunity to meet fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Slow resort breakfast — full Balinese spread with rice porridge, fresh papaya, and jamu herbal drink (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.lunch: Casual beachside café — club sandwich or tuna poke bowl (~IDR 90,000–150,000)
meals.dinner: Popular local restaurant — shared plates of tempeh manis, urap salad, and grilled corn (~IDR 150,000–230,000)

day_by_day.notes: This is your midpoint rest day. Don't feel guilty about doing less — a balanced trip means balancing activity with recovery.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip to a nearby island (such as Nusa Penida, Nusa Lembongan, or Gili Islands depending on proximity) — book a day tour (~IDR 350,000–600,000 including boat transfer and snorkeling gear). Snorkel with manta rays or vibrant coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot or by rented scooter. Visit iconic spots such as Kelingking Beach cliff viewpoint, Angel's Billabong, or Broken Beach (if visiting Nusa Penida).
day_by_day.evening: Return boat to the main island by late afternoon. Relax at the resort and enjoy a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before boat departure
meals.lunch: Island warung — fresh grilled fish, rice, and vegetables (~IDR 70,000–120,000)
meals.dinner: Resort or nearby restaurant — prawn curry with jasmine rice and mango lassi (~IDR 160,000–260,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book island day tours through your resort or a reputable local agency. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed for the boat. Wear water shoes for rocky beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Attend a 2-hour morning yoga workshop or retreat session at a dedicated yoga center — many in Bali offer specialized workshops in Yin Yoga, Pranayama breathwork, or meditation (~IDR 200,000–350,000). A deeply restorative experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local art gallery or cultural center to learn about Balinese Hindu traditions, batik fabric making, or silver jewelry crafting. Try a short hands-on workshop (~IDR 150,000–250,000).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a rooftop restaurant with panoramic views of the ocean or rice fields. Enjoy live traditional Balinese music if available.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga breakfast — banana, granola, and herbal tea (~IDR 40,000–70,000)
meals.lunch: Healthy café near the yoga center — Buddha bowl or green smoothie and wrap (~IDR 90,000–150,000)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant — slow-roasted lamb or mushroom risotto with local wine or Bintang beer (~IDR 200,000–320,000)

day_by_day.notes: Bring your own yoga mat if you have one, or rent one at the studio (~IDR 20,000–30,000). Wear comfortable, breathable yoga attire.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local morning market (pasar pagi) — wake up early to see the vibrant colors of tropical fruits, flowers, and spices. A fantastic cultural and photographic experience. Buy fresh fruit for a healthy snack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon — rent a kayak or outrigger canoe and paddle along the coastline (~IDR 100,000–200,000/hour). Alternatively, take a certified PADI discover scuba diving introductory session (~IDR 800,000–1,200,000).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Balinese cooking class in the evening (~IDR 350,000–500,000) — learn to make satay, tempeh, and black rice pudding. Eat your creation for dinner!

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit from the morning market + local bakery roti (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.lunch: Beachside café — grilled chicken skewers, corn on the cob, and coconut shake (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.dinner: Your own cooking class creation — a memorable and delicious experience!

day_by_day.notes: Morning markets typically open at 5–7am and wind down by 9am. Bring small denomination cash. The cooking class dinner counts as your evening activity and meal.

day_by_day.morning: Hike or trek to a scenic viewpoint — depending on your resort location, options include Mount Batur volcano sunrise trek (requires very early start, ~3am departure, ~IDR 300,000–500,000 guided) or a shorter coastal cliff walk for sunrise views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning exertion, enjoy a full afternoon of pure beach relaxation — swim, sunbathe, read, and enjoy the warm 25°C weather. Treat yourself to a fresh coconut on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style splurge dinner at one of Bali's renowned mid-to-upper-range restaurants — enjoy a multi-course Balinese tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: On the mountain (if doing Batur trek) — packed breakfast provided by tour, or post-hike warung breakfast
meals.lunch: Beachside — light snack of fresh fruit, coconut, and cold drink (~IDR 50,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Upscale local restaurant — Balinese tasting menu with suckling pig, duck, and tropical desserts (~IDR 300,000–500,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If doing the Mount Batur sunrise trek, book a certified guide at least 2 days in advance. Bring a warm layer as it's cool at the summit (around 10–15°C at 4am).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning yoga session on the beach — a mindful and reflective practice to honor your Bali journey. Journal your experiences, set intentions to carry the Bali spirit home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping for souvenirs, local crafts, and gifts — visit a local art market or boutique shops near the resort. Look for hand-carved wooden items, batik textiles, silver jewelry, and local coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop or beachfront bar — a classic Bali bucket-list experience. Toast to an incredible trip. Final dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip or try something new.

meals.breakfast: Slow resort breakfast — enjoy every bite, it's your last full day! (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.lunch: Local warung — your favorite Balinese dish one last time (~IDR 60,000–100,000)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant — seafood BBQ platter, Bintang beer, and coconut panna cotta for dessert (~IDR 200,000–300,000)

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully — wooden items and liquids have airline restrictions. Keep essentials in your carry-on for early departure if needed. Check out procedures with the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up for one last sunrise on the beach. Enjoy a peaceful breakfast at the resort. Complete checkout formalities and pack final items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, either relax at the resort pool for a final swim, or head to the airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure for check-in, immigration, and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali with wonderful memories of beaches, yoga, culture, and warm Balinese hospitality. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — treat yourself to the full spread (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or lounge — light meal before boarding (~IDR 100,000–200,000)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details the night before. Arrange airport transfer through the resort or pre-book a reliable driver. Carry some IDR cash for last-minute tips and airport snacks. Om Swastiastu — may your journey be blessed!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali's Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, Bali.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront suite. Enjoy a welcome drink and resort orientation. Take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to acclimatize and soak in the warm 25°C Bali sunshine.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, watching the golden hour over the Indian Ocean. Gentle welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light refreshments upon arrival at the resort — tropical fruit platter, fresh coconut water, and artisan sandwiches served by the pool
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the resort's signature beachfront restaurant — grilled Jimbaran-style seafood platter, sautéed local vegetables, steamed jasmine rice, and a curated Balinese dessert selection paired with a premium Balinese arak cocktail

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in if possible. Ensure resort concierge is briefed on your yoga and beach interests so they can pre-book sessions and beach cabanas for the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the resort's private beach deck with a certified instructor — a 90-minute Vinyasa flow class as the sun rises over the ocean. Follow with a refreshing dip in the resort's infinity pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort's exclusive beachfront cabana. Enjoy a 60-minute Balinese massage at the resort spa, followed by snorkeling in the calm coastal waters near the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachside dinner under the stars — a curated five-course tasting menu set directly on the sand with torchlight ambiance and live acoustic Balinese music.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant — freshly pressed tropical juices, acai bowls, eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, and Balinese black rice porridge
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled prawn skewers, avocado salad, cold-pressed juices, and a coconut sorbet
meals.dinner: Private beachside five-course dinner — amuse-bouche, seared tuna tataki, lobster bisque, pan-seared barramundi with lemongrass beurre blanc, and a passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Book the beachside dinner experience at least 24 hours in advance through the resort concierge. SPF 50+ sunscreen recommended for afternoon beach time.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Yin Yoga and meditation session at the resort's open-air jungle pavilion, led by a resident wellness guru. Focus on breathwork and mindfulness to deepen your Bali experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided excursion to the iconic Tanah Lot Sea Temple — a UNESCO-recognized cultural landmark perched dramatically on a coastal rock formation. Enjoy exclusive access with a knowledgeable private guide explaining Balinese Hindu traditions.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a traditional Kecak fire dance performance arranged privately for guests, followed by dinner at a premium beachfront restaurant nearby.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast served on your private terrace — fresh tropical fruit platter, smoked salmon bagels, barista-crafted coffee, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium warung near Tanah Lot — slow-braised Babi Guling (suckling pig), steamed rice, mixed satay platter, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sundara Beach Club, Jimbaran — wood-fired seafood, premium sashimi selection, and signature cocktails with ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is most dramatic at sunset but visiting in the afternoon avoids peak crowds. Wear modest clothing (sarong required) for temple entry — the resort can provide these.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) lesson on the calm coastal waters near the resort, guided by a certified water sports instructor. Follow with a 45-minute restorative yoga stretch on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day excursion to Uluwatu — visit the dramatic clifftop Uluwatu Temple perched 70 meters above the Indian Ocean. Explore hidden limestone coves and pristine surf beaches below the cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive sunset Kecak fire dance performance at Uluwatu Temple's open-air amphitheater with a private reserved front-row seating arrangement. Return to resort for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Poolside breakfast buffet at the resort — freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit selection, made-to-order omelets, and premium Bali Kintamani single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Single Fin Uluwatu — panoramic cliff-top views, fresh fish tacos, grilled calamari, and craft cocktails
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's rooftop terrace restaurant — slow-roasted duck confit with Balinese spice rub, grilled asparagus, truffle mashed potato, and a premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Uluwatu at least 30 minutes before the Kecak performance. Watch for mischievous monkeys at the temple — keep sunglasses and valuables secured.

day_by_day.morning: Full-morning luxury spa retreat at the resort — begin with a traditional Balinese boreh body scrub using turmeric, ginger, and rice bran, followed by a 90-minute hot stone massage and a floral bath ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon at the resort's private beach — enjoy water sports such as kayaking and snorkeling. Alternatively, relax in a private beachfront cabana with curated reading material and chilled beverages.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail cruise along the Bali coastline aboard a private catamaran — champagne, canapés, and panoramic views of the southern Bali coastline as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Healthy wellness breakfast at the spa café — green smoothie bowls, chia seed pudding, avocado toast on sourdough, and herbal detox teas
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the resort — freshly grilled lobster with garlic butter, mixed greens salad, chilled rosé wine, and tropical sorbets
meals.dinner: Post-cruise dinner at Sarong Restaurant, Seminyak — contemporary Asian-European fusion cuisine with an award-winning wine cellar; tasting menu with wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The sunset catamaran cruise must be booked 48 hours in advance. Bring a light wrap for the evening sea breeze. Sarong Restaurant requires smart casual attire.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga retreat at a clifftop yoga shala overlooking the ocean — a 2-hour immersive Ashtanga yoga session with a master teacher, incorporating pranayama and guided meditation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seminyak's luxury boutiques and art galleries — browse high-end Balinese fashion, handcrafted jewelry, and contemporary art. Visit Ku De Ta beach club for an afternoon refreshment.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Merah Putih Restaurant, Seminyak — one of Bali's most architecturally stunning restaurants, serving refined modern Indonesian cuisine in a dramatic bamboo cathedral setting.

meals.breakfast: Pre-yoga light breakfast — banana, almond butter, green tea, and a protein smoothie served at the yoga shala
meals.lunch: Brunch at Ku De Ta Beach Club — eggs royale, wagyu beef sliders, fresh oysters, and chilled Aperol spritz with ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Merah Putih — slow-cooked rendang beef cheek, crispy duck with sambal matah, black rice risotto, and a curated Indonesian wine and cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: Seminyak is approximately 20–30 minutes from the resort by private car. Arrange transportation through the resort concierge. Merah Putih reservation recommended 2 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Ubud — depart early by private luxury vehicle. Begin with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary and the iconic Ubud Royal Palace in the heart of Ubud town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Tegallalang UNESCO Rice Terraces — a breathtaking landscape of emerald green stepped paddies. Enjoy a private guided walk through the terraces with a local farmer guide. Visit a traditional Balinese healer (Balian) for an authentic wellness consultation.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ubud at Locavore Restaurant — one of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, celebrating hyper-local Balinese ingredients with a world-class tasting menu. Overnight stay at the resort upon return.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — continental spread with fresh juices, yogurt parfait, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Swept Away Restaurant, COMO Shambhala Estate, Ubud — organic farm-to-table cuisine in a stunning jungle riverside setting; grilled fish, seasonal vegetables, and fresh herb salads
meals.dinner: Dinner at Locavore, Ubud — 7-course tasting menu featuring hyper-seasonal, locally foraged ingredients with optional wine or juice pairing

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1.5 hours from the resort. Depart by 8:00 AM to maximize the day. Locavore reservation must be made weeks in advance — have the concierge arrange this at the start of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — gentle beach yoga flow at sunrise on the resort's private beach. Follow with a slow, mindful breakfast and a 60-minute reflexology session at the resort spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat trip to Nusa Lembongan Island — explore crystal-clear waters, vibrant coral reefs, and pristine white sand beaches. Enjoy snorkeling with manta rays at Manta Point (seasonal).
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a private couples' or solo sunset dinner on your villa terrace — a bespoke menu prepared and served by a dedicated butler.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast on the resort terrace — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, freshly baked croissants, tropical fruit platter, and a Balinese specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Beach BBQ lunch on Nusa Lembongan — freshly grilled reef fish, prawn satay, coconut rice, and chilled tropical juices
meals.dinner: In-villa private dinner — butter-poached king prawns, beef tenderloin with truffle jus, roasted seasonal vegetables, and a chocolate lava cake with vanilla bean ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The boat trip to Nusa Lembongan takes approximately 30–45 minutes. Book a private speedboat through the resort for the most comfortable experience. Bring waterproof sunscreen and reef-safe products.

day_by_day.morning: Morning surf lesson at a nearby premium surf school — professional instructors provide one-on-one coaching on beginner-friendly waves. Suitable for all skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Point Beach (Suluban Beach) near Uluwatu — a hidden gem accessible through limestone cave passages, with dramatic wave-carved cliffs and turquoise waters. Relax at the clifftop café overlooking the surf break.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at Cuca Restaurant, Jimbaran — a celebrated Bali fine-dining destination known for inventive tapas-style cuisine using local ingredients and bold flavors.

meals.breakfast: Energizing pre-surf breakfast at the resort — protein-rich eggs, whole-grain toast, fresh fruit, and a green smoothie
meals.lunch: Lunch at Blue Point Bay Villas café — light sandwiches, fresh salads, and coconut water with stunning cliff views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuca Restaurant — creative tapas including Balinese-spiced lamb ribs, truffle arancini, miso-glazed eggplant, and signature dessert cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons are best in the morning when winds are calmer. Suluban Beach requires a short walk down steep limestone steps — wear comfortable footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive Balinese cooking class at a premium culinary school near the resort — learn to prepare traditional dishes including lawar, sate lilit, and black rice pudding using fresh market ingredients sourced at dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a full afternoon of relaxation — enjoy the resort's infinity pool, read by the beach, or indulge in a 60-minute aromatherapy facial at the spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfire experience on the resort's beach — curated bonfire setup with premium Champagne, artisan cheese boards, and a private acoustic musician for a magical evening under Bali's stars.

meals.breakfast: Market-fresh breakfast at the cooking school — fresh tropical fruits, Balinese-style banana pancakes, and turmeric lattes
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class — a celebratory Balinese feast with your instructor and fellow participants
meals.dinner: Beachfire grazing dinner — artisan cheese and charcuterie boards, smoked seafood, bruschetta, and a curated Champagne and wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically includes a guided market visit — arrange an early departure (7:00 AM) to experience the morning market at its most vibrant.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise photography tour along the Bali coastline — capture dramatic cliff formations, hidden beaches, and local fishing boat scenes with a professional photography guide. Perfect for social media and personal memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Padang Padang Beach — one of Bali's most iconic and scenic beaches. Relax on the fine white sand, swim in the clear waters, and explore the rocky coastal landscape. Enjoy a premium beach club experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style luxury dinner at Métis Restaurant, Seminyak — a Bali institution offering French-Mediterranean cuisine in a stunning colonial villa setting surrounded by rice paddies.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go pre-tour breakfast — fresh fruit, energy bars, and thermos coffee provided by the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Finn's Beach Club, Berawa — gourmet beach club fare including fresh sashimi, lobster rolls, and craft cocktails with a stunning pool and ocean backdrop
meals.dinner: Dinner at Métis Restaurant — foie gras terrine, pan-seared duck breast with cherry reduction, French onion soup, and a decadent crème brûlée with a premium Bordeaux wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The photography tour starts at 5:30 AM to catch the golden hour sunrise. Padang Padang Beach has a small entrance fee and is accessed via a narrow staircase through rock formations.

day_by_day.morning: Final yoga and wellness morning — a 2-hour transformational yoga and sound healing session at the resort's garden pavilion, incorporating Tibetan singing bowls, guided visualization, and breathwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping at Seminyak Square and Bali Collection — pick up premium Balinese textiles, handcrafted silver jewelry, artisan batik, and specialty Bali coffee and spices as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — a bespoke chef's table experience with a personalized 7-course menu created in consultation with the executive chef.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast — full hot and cold buffet with made-to-order waffles, fresh oysters, smoked salmon, premium cheeses, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a chic Seminyak café — avocado toast with poached eggs, beetroot salad, cold brew coffee, and a slice of raw vegan cheesecake
meals.dinner: Chef's table farewell dinner at the resort — personalized 7-course tasting menu with wine pairings, featuring the finest local and imported ingredients; concludes with a personalized dessert and Champagne toast

day_by_day.notes: Coordinate with the resort concierge to arrange the chef's table experience at least 3 days in advance. Begin packing this evening for an organized departure the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk along the resort's private shoreline — a peaceful, reflective stroll to conclude the Bali journey. Optional last yoga session or meditation by the water's edge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout (arrange with resort — typically available until 14:00 for premium guests). Enjoy a final pool session or spa treatment before departure. Private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali — carry the serenity, warmth, and memories of 13 extraordinary days on the Island of the Gods.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a celebratory spread on the private terrace with fresh tropical fruits, pastries, eggs to order, and a signature Bali farewell cocktail (or mocktail)
meals.lunch: Light pre-departure lunch at the resort — club sandwich, Caesar salad, fresh coconut water, and a scoop of artisan gelato
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. The resort concierge can arrange a private airport transfer. Ask the spa to prepare a travel wellness kit — essential oils, herbal teas, and a sleep mask — as a parting gift for the journey home.
